text: IT ASSET MANAGEMENT POLICY Company-issued laptops, monitors, and other equipment are assigned to employees based on role requirements. Employees are responsible for safeguarding assigned equipment. Lost, stolen, or damaged equipment must be reported to IT Operations immediately. Employees must return all assigned company equipment when leaving the organization. Employees must not transfer assigned equipment to another employee without IT approval. Asset assignment information is maintained in the company asset register.

EMPLOYEE EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT POLICY Employees may claim reimbursement for eligible business-related expenses. Meal expenses are reimbursable up to INR 250 per employee per day. Internet expenses for approved remote employees are reimbursable up to INR 1,000 per month. Travel expenses must be supported by valid receipts. Claims must be submitted through the finance portal within 30 days of the expense date. Claims above INR 10,000 require manager approval. Personal purchases and expenses without valid supporting documents are not reimbursable.

FINANCE FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Q: What is the daily meal reimbursement limit? A: Employees can claim meal expenses up to INR 300 per employee per day. Q: How long do employees have to submit reimbursement claims? A: Claims should be submitted within 30 days of the expense date. Q: Are receipts mandatory? A: Yes. Valid receipts must be attached to reimbursement claims. NOTE: This FAQ is marked current and has an effective date of 2026-02-01. Its meal reimbursement limit conflicts with the Employee Expense Reimbursement Policy. The conflict has intentionally been retained for testing.

ANNUAL LEAVE POLICY — 2024 Employees are entitled to 18 days of annual paid leave per calendar year. Leave requests must be submitted to the reporting manager at least 3 working days in advance. Unused annual leave can be carried forward up to a maximum of 5 days. This policy was superseded effective 2026-01-01. Do not use this document to answer current employee entitlement questions.

ANNUAL LEAVE POLICY — 2026 Employees are entitled to 20 days of annual paid leave per calendar year. Leave requests should be submitted through the HR portal at least 3 working days before the intended leave date. Unused annual leave can be carried forward up to a maximum of 7 days, subject to manager approval. Sick leave entitlement is 6 days per calendar year. This policy replaces the 2024 Annual Leave Policy.

EMPLOYEE ONBOARDING GUIDE New employees must complete the onboarding checklist during their first working week. The checklist includes: - Completing personal and employment information - Reviewing company policies - Completing mandatory security training - Setting up corporate email and collaboration tools - Confirming receipt of assigned equipment Employees should contact Human Resources for onboarding-related questions. IT access issues should be reported through the IT support ticketing process.

REMOTE WORK POLICY Eligible employees may work remotely with manager approval. Employees working remotely must: - Remain available during agreed working hours. - Protect confidential company information. - Use approved company devices and secure network connections. - Follow information security requirements. Employees must obtain manager approval before making changes to their agreed work arrangement. Approved remote employees may claim internet expenses subject to the Employee Expense Reimbursement Policy.

INFORMATION SECURITY INCIDENT PROCEDURE Employees must immediately report suspected security incidents. Examples include: - Phishing emails - Lost or stolen company devices - Unauthorized access - Accidental exposure of confidential information Employees should raise a high-priority IT security ticket. Employees must not share passwords or authentication codes. Security incidents involving suspected data exposure must be escalated to the Information Security team. Employees should not investigate suspected breaches independently or delete potential evidence.

BUSINESS TRAVEL POLICY Business travel must be approved by the employee's reporting manager before booking. Employees should use approved travel booking channels wherever available. Reasonable transport and accommodation expenses incurred for approved business travel may be reimbursed. Employees must retain receipts and submit expense claims within 30 days of the expense date. Personal travel expenses and unapproved upgrades are not reimbursable. Travel reimbursement is subject to the Employee Expense Reimbursement Policy.
